complexity.notes: h is the main tree's height; a skewed generalized tree would hit CPython's recursion limit, an iterative or explicit-stack version avoids that. Worst case is quadratic because repeated values let the equality check run deep at every node; ||serializing both trees and searching for one in the other, or hashing each subtree bottom-up (Merkle-style)||, brings this down to O(n + m). The benchmark's distinct values make every non-matching check fail on its first comparison, so only the O(n) traversal is measured.
complexity.summary: Recursively walks the main tree and, at every node, runs a structural-equality check against subRoot, returning true on the first full match. The equality helper short-circuits on the first value or shape mismatch.
